pageTitle: Guitar Capos: Mechanical Physics, Radius Matching & Harmonic Transposition
subtitle: Master clamping mechanics, fretboard radius matching, intonation stabilization, and partial capo tunings

introduction.title: The Capo: Acoustic Transposition & Scale Length Physics
introduction.text: A capo (derived from the Italian 'capotasto', meaning 'head of the fretboard') is far more than a transposition crutch for guitarists who avoid barre chords. It is a precision mechanical clamp that physically shortens the vibrating scale length of the instrument, raising the fundamental pitch of all strings simultaneously while preserving open-string resonance and ringing open-chord voicings. By altering string length without changing mechanical string tension at the tuning pegs, a capo transforms the acoustic timbre of the instrument: the tone becomes tighter, crisper, and more bell-like, resembling a mandolin or harpsichord as it climbs the neck. In the hands of master songwriters—from Joni Mitchell and James Taylor to Tommy Emmanuel—the capo is a profound compositional instrument.
introduction.quote: A capo changes not only the key, but the harmonic timbre, string excursion, and resonance profile of the entire instrument.

columns.title: Clamping Mechanics & Pitch Drift Physics
columns.text: When a guitarist frets a note with a finger, the fleshy pad cushions the string directly behind the fret crown with just enough downward force to contact the metal wire. A poorly designed capo clamps down with excessive mechanical brute force, stretching the strings downward into the fretboard trough. Because the string is pinned between nut and bridge, this downward deflection stretches the steel core, increasing mechanical tension and pulling the guitar sharp by 10 to 25 cents. Precision capos utilize micrometer tension screws or adaptive silicone pads to apply the absolute minimum force required to achieve clear, buzz-free tone without pitch drift.

columns.title: Fretboard Radius Matching
columns.text: Guitar fingerboards are not flat; they feature a cylindrical or conical radius ranging from 7.25" (vintage Fender) and 9.5"–12" (modern electrics) to 16" (acoustic dreadnoughts) and flat (classical nylon guitars). If a flat-padded capo is clamped across a 7.25" vintage neck, the outer E strings are crushed with violent force while the middle D and G strings buzz. Conversely, clamping a curved capo onto a classical guitar crushes the center strings and leaves the outer E strings unmuted. Matching capo pad curvature to fretboard radius is mandatory for intonation stability.

cards.title: Micrometer Screw Tension (Shubb, Planet Waves)
cards.description: The gold standard for professional touring musicians, studio sessions, and intonation purists.

fields.label: Mechanical Principle
fields.value: A fine-threaded knurled thumbscrew adjusts an over-center cam lever, allowing the player to calibrate exact clamping pressure to the millinewton.

fields.label: Zero Pitch Drift
fields.value: Allows dialing in the exact pressure required to eliminate buzz without deflecting strings into the fret space, keeping chords perfectly in tune.

fields.label: Neck Versatility
fields.value: Seamlessly adapts to ultra-thin shred necks, thick vintage 1950s 'baseball bat' profiles, and 12-string guitars.

fields.label: Benchmark Models
fields.value: Shubb C1 Deluxe, D'Addario Planet Waves NS Pro Capo

cards.title: Spring-Loaded Trigger (Kyser, Dunlop)
cards.description: The ubiquitous live-performance workhorse engineered for lightning-fast one-handed position changes.

fields.label: Mechanical Principle
fields.value: A heavy-duty internal steel coil spring provides fixed, instant clamping force upon release.

fields.label: Speed & Convenience
fields.value: Can be repositioned or clamped onto the headstock in less than two seconds between songs during high-energy live shows.

fields.label: Tension Limitation
fields.value: Fixed spring tension cannot be adjusted; on guitars with tall frets or light strings, it can pull notes noticeably sharp, requiring quick retuning.

fields.label: Benchmark Models
fields.value: Kyser Quick-Change, Dunlop Trigger Capo

cards.title: Adaptive Radius Technology (G7th Performance 3)
cards.description: Modern engineering breakthrough featuring self-adjusting silicone pads that contour to any neck curvature.

fields.label: ART Architecture
fields.value: Adaptive Radius Technology (ART) houses sub-dermal articulated silicone cells that automatically deform to match any fretboard radius (from 7.25" to flat).

fields.label: Squeeze-On Clutch
fields.value: Internal patented clutch mechanism: squeeze with hand to clamp; press release lever to detach. Zero screws, zero spring fatigue.

fields.label: Benchmark Models
fields.value: G7th Performance 3, G7th Heritage (yoke style)

cards.title: Yoke / Cradle Style (Paige, G7th Heritage)
cards.description: Traditional bluegrass and acoustic flatpicking cradle design applying symmetrical, center-pull pressure.

fields.label: Symmetrical Pull
fields.value: A metal cradle completely encloses the neck, with a center-mounted thumbscrew pulling directly from the rear centerline, eliminating lateral string displacement.

fields.label: Behind-the-Nut Storage
fields.value: When not in use, the capo slides up behind the nut on the headstock, remaining permanently mounted to the guitar.

fields.label: Benchmark Models
fields.value: Paige Clik Capo, G7th Heritage Yoke Capo

cards.title: The 'Right Behind the Fret' Rule
cards.description: Over 90% of capo tuning complaints are caused by improper placement rather than the capo itself.

fields.label: Correct Positioning
fields.value: Place the capo pad directly behind the fret crown (within 1 to 2 mm), perfectly parallel to the fretwire. This ensures the fret crown acts as the physical nut with zero downward string bending.

fields.label: Mid-Fret Disaster
fields.value: Clamping in the center between two frets forces the string to bridge an air gap, bending the string into a steep V-shape that pulls every note sharp by up to 20 cents.

fields.label: On-Top Muting
fields.value: Placing the rubber pad directly on top of the metal fret wire dampens string vibration, killing acoustic sustain and high-frequency harmonics.

cards.title: Lateral Pull & Post-Capo Fine Tuning
cards.description: Preventing accidental sideways string displacement during clamping.

fields.label: Avoid Lateral Bending
fields.value: When clamping, do not pull or drag the capo sideways across the neck, as this bends strings across the fretwire and locks them in a sharp, bent position.

fields.label: String Re-Seating Trick
fields.value: After clamping, give each string a gentle, micro-tug upward with your right hand. This allows the string to equalize tension across the rubber pad and fret crown.

fields.label: Sweetened Tuning Check
fields.value: Always verify tuning with a strobe tuner (Peterson StroboClip HD) after applying a capo. The low E and B strings are the most prone to sharpness.

sections.title: Partial Capos: The Secret World of Pseudo-Open Tunings

cards.title: The Esus / DADGAD Cut Capo
cards.description: Clamping strings 5, 4, and 3 at the 2nd fret while leaving strings 6, 2, and 1 open.

fields.label: The Sonic Illusion
fields.value: Produces the open notes E-B-E-A-B-E. Gives standard-tuned guitars the sweeping Celtic resonance, open drones, and modal majesty of DADGAD tuning.

fields.label: Standard Fingerings Intact
fields.value: Because strings 6, 2, and 1 remain in standard tuning, you can play familiar standard scales and bass lines behind and above the capo without retuning your pegs.

fields.label: Pioneering Artists
fields.value: David Wilcox, Trace Bundy, Antoine Dufour, Phil Keaggy.

cards.title: Drop-D & Spider Capo Systems
cards.description: Independent per-string clamping systems that unlock infinite harmonic permutations.

fields.label: Drop-D Capo
fields.value: Clamps strings 5 through 1 at the 2nd fret, leaving the 6th string open. Simulates Drop-D tuning raised to E (E-B-E-G#-B-E), delivering massive low-end acoustic drive.

fields.label: The Spider Capo
fields.value: Features six individual mechanical finger levers over each string. Allows guitarists to clamp any custom permutation (e.g., fretting strings 1, 3, and 5 while leaving 2, 4, and 6 open).

fields.label: Harmonic Exploration
fields.value: Allows playing open chord drones with melodies fretted both above and behind the capoed positions simultaneously.
